newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaragua bids to move kids from street to school.
newsitem.headline: Nicaragua bids to move kids from street to school.

text.p: Nicaragua announced on Monday the start of an ambitious plan to remove hundreds of children who beg and sell at Managua's major intersections and put them back in school.

In the plan, coordinated by the state-run Nicaraguan Fund for Children and the Family (Fonif), government workers will visit the parents of "stoplight children," as they are known, and counsel them to keep their children in school, President Arnoldo Aleman told a news conference.
Children without parents, or whose parents send them to the stoplights to earn money, will be placed in special youth training centres, Fonif director Fanny Montenegro said.
Aleman said the government was in the process of locating and equipping such centres, which will "give care, love and Christian education to the children."
"The short term objective is to attend to the needs of children at risk at the city's streetlights in such a way that they abandon these risky activities and go back to school," Montenegro said.

The plan met with sharp criticism from non-governmental groups working with street children in Nicaragua, who said it was a superficial attempt to "clean up" the streets without addressing the underlying poverty that causes parents to send their children to the streets to earn money.

Aleman said a government census found 647 street children selling, begging or stealing at Managua's major intersections, 153 of them girls. He said 15 percent of the children had been completely abandoned by their parents and 60 percent did not attend school.
